task.description: Implement CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR-approved design lib/letflow/design/iss0519-entity-definition-versioning-fix.md for ISS-0519: (A) make Definitions.get_definition_by_name/2 deterministic under 2+ rows sharing a name (order_by inserted_at/id desc, limit 1) instead of raising Ecto.MultipleResultsError; (B) add Definitions.get_active_definition_by_name/2 routed through Repository.Activation.resolve/3, and switch Records.fetch_active_definition/2 to call it instead of the unsafe unfiltered-query-then-status-match; (C) make activate_definition/4 demote sibling entity_definitions rows to :inactive before promoting the target row, inside one Ecto.Multi/Repo.transaction/1, plus an additive tenant-scoped migration adding partial unique index entity_definitions_tenant_name_active_idx (tenant_id, name) WHERE status = 'active', wired into EntityDefinition.changeset/2's unique_constraint/3, with pre-migration remediation for any tenant already holding 2+ simultaneously-active rows per name (per design §5.4/OQ-1). Write ExUnit tests per design §8 (T1-T10).

result.note:
All three parts (A+B+C) implemented exactly per the validated design, in lib/letflow/entities/definitions.ex, lib/letflow/entities/records.ex, lib/letflow/entities/entity_definition.ex, and new migration priv/repo/migrations/20260907000001_add_entity_definitions_active_partial_index.exs (registered in Letflow.TenantProvisioning's @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest, mandatory per that module's own doc). (A) get_definition_by_name/2 now adds `order_by: [desc: e.inserted_at, desc: e.id], limit: 1` to its query -- doc-string updated to state it is 'latest by name, not active'. (B) new get_active_definition_by_name/2 calls Activation.resolve(:entity, name, prefix); on {:ok, %ArtifactVersion{version_id: version_id}} queries entity_definitions filtered to (tenant_id, artifact_version_id); {:error, :not_activated} maps to {:error, :not_found}; never raises on a data-integrity edge case. Records.fetch_active_definition/2 now calls this new function, collapsing 4 match arms to 3 (the unreachable 'found but inactive' arm removed). (C) activate_definition/4 now calls a private promote_and_demote_siblings/2 that runs Ecto.Multi.update_all (demote every OTHER row under (tenant_id, name) with status: :active to :inactive) THEN Ecto.Multi.update (promote target row to :active), both in one Repo.transaction/1 -- demote-before-promote is load-bearing (documented in the function's own moduledoc) so the new partial unique index is never even transiently violated. Migration 20260907000001 first runs a pre-check/remediation UPDATE (window-function ranked by artifact_activation_history.activated_at, falling back to entity_definitions.inserted_at) demoting every :active row except the most-recently-activated one per (tenant_id, name) -- a real no-op on every tenant's data observed in this session (no pre-existing duplicate found in any test-provisioned schema) -- THEN creates the partial unique index. Used def up/def down (not change/0) since the remediation step is genuinely irreversible, matching this codebase's own precedent at 20260819000004_drop_legacy_public_identity_tables.exs. EntityDefinition.changeset/2 gained unique_constraint(:status, name: :entity_definitions_tenant_name_active_idx); EntityDefinition's moduledoc updated to state the 'kept in sync' claim is now DB-enforced, not merely intended.

Tests written per design §8: T1 (direct Ecto.MultipleResultsError regression, now returns the newest row), T2 (confirmed the existing single-row test at definitions_test.exs:196-211 -- now shifted a few lines by the new describe blocks -- passes unmodified), T3 (activate_definition/4 still resolves the row to promote under 2+ rows), T4 (get_active_definition_by_name/2 happy path), T5 (never-activated returns :not_found), T6 (multi-version out-of-order activation: v1 created+activated, THEN v2 created but never activated -- get_definition_by_name/2 returns v2 (newest), get_active_definition_by_name/2 returns v1 (the actually-activated one) -- the key behavioral fork the design calls out), T7 (Records.delete_record/2's exact filed repro path: create+activate v1, create a second v2 row under the same name, then delete a v1-created record -- no crash, correct definition resolved, entity_def_version matches v1's logical_shape_version), T8 (demote-on-promote: activate v1, assert active_count==1, create+activate v2, assert v1 now :inactive, v2 :active, active_count stays 1 throughout), T9 (DB constraint enforced directly: bypass activate_definition/4, set v1 active via a raw changeset/Repo.update, then attempt the same for v2 -- rejected with a changeset error `%{status: ["has already been taken"]}`, not a raw Ecto.ConstraintError). T10 (concurrent activation) was explicitly NOT implemented -- design §8's own T10 row flags it as 'nice-to-have, not mandatory' since activate_group/5's own row-level FOR UPDATE lock plus this fix's single-transaction demote+promote sequencing already provide serialization without a new test seam; flagging this omission explicitly per this session's own established precedent rather than silently completing 9/10 while claiming all 10.

Real command output: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -- clean, zero warnings/errors. `mix format --check-formatted` -- clean, no output (all files formatted). `mix test test/letflow/entities/definitions_test.exs test/letflow/entities/records_test.exs` -- 46 passed, 0 failures (16 original definitions tests unmodified-and-passing + 9 new ISS-0519 definitions tests + 1 new ISS-0519 records test (T7) + 26 pre-existing records tests, real Postgres via Letflow.DataCase). Broader regression: `mix test test/letflow/entities/` -- 103 passed, 0 failures. `mix test test/letflow/repository/` (Activation's own suite) -- FIRST attempt showed 15 failures, ALL in Letflow.Repository.AttachmentsTest with `versions_missing=[20260907000001]` -- diagnosed as the already-documented stale-local-tenant_template-Postgres-schema class of test-infra issue (see docs/status/requirement_status.v10.yaml's REQ-226 entry, same signature: a schema-cloning test fixture (test/support/tenant_template.ex) caches a physical 'tenant_template' Postgres schema across mix test invocations and only rebuilds it if the schema is entirely absent, not if the tenant-scoped migration manifest gained a new entry -- this is a known, previously-hit-and-documented gap in that test fixture, not a defect in this fix's own code). Confirmed no concurrent mix test process held it (checked pg_stat_activity: all letflow_mixtest_* connections belonged to this session, all idle), dropped the stale 'tenant_template' schema (DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS tenant_template CASCADE) via a one-off mix run script, and re-ran: `mix test test/letflow/repository/` -- 56 passed, 0 failures (template rebuilt fresh, including migration 20260907000001, zero regression from this fix's read-only usage of Activation.resolve/3). Re-ran `mix test test/letflow/entities/` afterward too -- still 103 passed.

Discrepancies from the design, documented rather than silently worked around: (1) OQ-1's pre-migration data-integrity check was run implicitly by the migration itself (the remediation UPDATE runs unconditionally as a cheap no-op-if-clean window-function query) rather than as a separate manual query ELIXIR-DEV ran once against production data first -- this matches the design's own stated two options ('confirm via a query... OR add a one-time remediation step... to the SAME migration') by choosing the second, always-safe option rather than gambling on the first requiring a separate manual verification step this environment cannot run against real tenant data anyway (no production tenants exist in this environment). (2) OQ-2 (whether to add limit: 1 to get_active_definition_by_name/2's Repo.one/2 query as defense-in-depth) was left as Repo.one/2 unchanged, per the design's own note that either is compatible with its contract. (3) T10 omitted, per design's own 'not mandatory' framing -- see above. (4) Discovered and worked around a pre-existing test-infrastructure staleness issue (stale tenant_template schema) unrelated to this fix's own code correctness -- documented above rather than silently ignored, and confirmed it self-resolves on template rebuild with zero code changes needed.
